question: A resting heart rate of 110 beats per minute is within the normal range for a healthy 2-year-old child but would represent a tachycardia requiring investigation in a healthy 12-year-old.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Normal heart rate decreases progressively with age throughout childhood. Always interpret paediatric vital signs against age-specific reference ranges — never apply adult norms to children.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Normal paediatric heart rate ranges are age-dependent: neonate 110-160 bpm; infant 90-150; toddler (1-3 yr) 80-130 bpm; preschool (3-5 yr) 80-120; school-age (6-12 yr) 70-110; adolescent 60-100 bpm. A heart rate of 110 bpm is well within normal for a 2-year-old but at the upper limit or mildly elevated for a 12-year-old at rest, warranting clinical assessment.
